applicable_when: The kernel loads in_ptr0 with address pattern `x0 + 3136*r0_2 + 301056*x1`. Adjacent threads differ in x0 (stride-1, contiguous), but the reduction loop iterates r0_2 with stride 3136 elements (12544 bytes). This is an NCHW->NHWC transpose where the channel dimension (C=96) is the reduction axis but is stored non-contiguously (stride=HW=3136). Each warp issues 32 separate cache-line transactions instead of 1, causing the 1/32 sector utilization. Additionally, R0_BLOCK=512 is 5.3x larger than r0_numel=96, wasting shared memory and limiting occupancy to 3 blocks/SM. Reducing R0_BLOCK to 96 (exact fit) and tuning XBLOCK via autotune will: (1) reduce shared memory per block -> more blocks/SM -> higher occupancy, (2) allow the scheduler to hide L1TEX latency with more active warps.
